claims.text: Controlled thermal treatment of the metastable solid solution will induce nucleation and growth of fine intermetallic phases.
The thermally formed intermetallics can include Ti-rich Ti2Zn.
Mg-Ti-Zn multi-principal-element alloys tend to form intermetallic compounds such as Ti2Zn, Mg21Zn25, and TiZn16.
Ti-rich intermetallic precipitates serve as nucleation sites for a TiO2-rich surface film.
Thermal energy mobilizes solute atoms and thereby causes precipitation of fine intermetallic phases.
Ti-containing Mg-Ti-Zn alloy can develop a TiO2-rich surface film.
A TiO2-rich surface film enhances passivation and lowers corrosion current density.
Fine and uniformly distributed intermetallics promote formation of a coherent TiO2 film.
The TiO2-rich film retards high-temperature oxidation.
Excessive thermal exposure causes intermetallic coarsening and formation of interconnected intermetallic networks.
Intermetallics can establish micro-galvanic effects with the Mg-rich matrix.
Coarsening of intermetallics increases micro-galvanic corrosion and undermines passivation.
Intermetallic coarsening degrades high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Optimal annealing will produce corrosion resistance similar to or better than that of the initial metastable state.
Optimal annealing will produce high-temperature oxidation resistance similar to or better than that of the initial metastable state.
Excessive thermal exposure will yield coarse intermetallics, observable micro-galvanic corrosion, and decreased corrosion resistance.
The initial metastable solid solution lacks significant intermetallic precipitates and a defined passivating oxide layer.
A critical temperature-time boundary separates beneficial fine precipitation from deleterious coarsening.
The precipitation-to-coarsening threshold depends on composition and processing history.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits corrosion or oxidation resistance merely similar to the initial state, whereas the falsification rule requires enhanced resistance; an unchanged result could therefore both satisfy the prediction and trigger falsification.
